title: Short Stuff: The Berners Street Hoax
summary: Short Stuff hoax edition on the Berners Street hoax of November 1810 in London. Josh and Chuck describe Theodore Hook, who bet his friend Samuel Beasley he could make 54 Berners Street the talk of London within a week. On the day, a flood of tradespeople, servants, and officials (including the Lord Mayor, the Archbishop of Canterbury, and the Duke of York) arrived at the house in response to fake summons and orders, shutting down the street. Hook was widely assumed to be the culprit and later claimed credit in his semi-autobiographical novel Gilbert Gurney, though he was never prosecuted. The hosts close by raising the possibility that the hoax never actually happened and was only a hoax in newspaper reports.

segments.title: Introduction and setup of the bet
segments.summary: Josh introduces the hoax edition and sets up Theodore Hook, a mischievous 22-year-old, and his friend Samuel Beasley walking past 54 Berners Street in November 1810, where Hook bets he can make the house famous within a week.

segments.title: Chimney sweeps arrive
segments.summary: A week later, a chimney sweep arrives at 54 Berners Street asking to clean Mrs Tottenham's chimney, and the servants send him away. More sweeps follow, and the hosts pause on a cliffhanger.

segments.title: Flood of tradespeople and officials
segments.summary: A long list of tradespeople, servants, and others arrive at the house, drawn by fake summons, and gawkers crowd the street until police shut it down. Officials including the Lord Mayor of London, the Archbishop of Canterbury, the Governor of the Bank of England, the chairman of the East India Company, and the Duke of York are also drawn in.

segments.title: Aftermath, attribution, and Gilbert Gurney
segments.summary: The hoax made newspapers across England and was recorded in annual registers. Hook was widely assumed to be responsible and later claimed credit in the novel Gilbert Gurney, but he was never prosecuted. The hosts note his letter-writing helpers and that he chose the house at random.

segments.title: Hoax on a hoax theory
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a theory that the event may never have actually happened, since the reports came from newspapers rather than eyewitnesses, making the real hoax Hook's invented story.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck closes the episode and the show credits iHeartRadio.
